body:
rafa: Quick sync 1: we keep losing billing attribution when the sampler runs before async enrichment. We saw ~0.3% untagged traces in last 24h.

elaine: Can you outline how those traces flow? Which proxies?

rafa: Mostly mobile + legacy edge in ap-south. Proxy emits minimal spans immediately, enrichment service (async) attaches tenant/billing later. Sampler often drops the early span.

tom: Options I see: 1) enrich synchronously (adds voip latency), 2) attach a derived token so sampler can decide, 3) write a transient stitch record keyed by trace id.

neda: Derived token = HMAC(token, proxy_salt) included as header. Sampler checks HMAC to decide keep/drop. Enricher looks up raw token from internal store if needed.

rafa: HMAC approach is appealing because it avoids a write-heavy path. But we need salt management, and older SDKs won't add the header.

elaine: For SDK/backcompat we can gate: if header present -> HMAC flow; else -> beacon fallback write. That keeps the KV writes limited to the minority.

ops-bot: note: deploy canary proxy v1.5 -> ap-south-1 :rocket:

tom: Beacon design: setex('stitch:'+trace_id, TTL=12, ciphertext(billing_id)). Use idempotent write so retries don't blow up. Evict by LRU and cap shard size.

neda: Security: never store plaintext. Use envelope encryption with KMS-wrapped key, short TTL, and audit on decryption. Add masking in logs.

rafa: Perf numbers from a micro-spike: beacon writes @ 3k/s is fine on a two-node redis. But we should cap writes per-tenant and track hot-keys.

elaine: What about including a tenant-hash in the span header (non-reversible) so sampler can do deterministic sampling by tenant without KMS? Cheaper but less flexible.

tom: If we HMAC billing_id -> header, sampler can run simple check: if HMAC_valid and tenant in keep-list -> keep. Otherwise normal random. That gives us deterministic keep for important accounts.

metrics-bot: metric emit: stitch.beacon_write_rate, stitch.hit_rate, stitch.missed_count, sampler.hmac_accepted_rate

neda: We must also think about consent/regulatory leakage. Even derived tokens must be treated as PII-equivalent in some regions. Put them behind access controls.

rafa: Actionable plan: 1) canary HMAC header on proxies in ap-south for 48h (tom + infra) 2) prototype beacon fallback (elaine) 3) security sign-off on key handling (neda) 4) dashboards + alerting (metrics) -> ticket P-5012.

tom: I'll push a small spike and surface p50/p95 for proxy latency and stitch write rates.

elaine: I'll stub the beacon in staging using setex + AES-GCM. Keep TTL 12s for now.

neda: I'll start the security checklist and list KMS rotation cadence. We should fail-closed if we detect mismatches during enrichment.

rafa: Please add a guardrail: if missed_billing_count spikes >0.05% over 10m, auto-enable beacon fallback for that region.

metrics-bot: alert rule created: A-TRC-14 "stitch missed billing >0.05%" -> notify #oncall-platform

tom: timeline: spike + canary telemetry within 36h.

elaine: ok. I'll open a short RFC summarizing tradeoffs and include perf numbers and the fallback flow.

rafa: thanks all. We'll reconvene after canary.

ops-bot: ticket created P-5012 "stitching: HMAC header + beacon fallback" assigned -> eng-platform

rafa: small reminder: update the ingestion SLA notes; stitch lookups add small tail latency (tracking).
